gloss: to have one's attention drawn away; to be distracted

definitions.gloss: to have one's attention taken by something; to be distracted
definitions.explanation: For something to pull one's attention away, so that what one should have been watching gets neglected. Literally 'to have one's attention taken.' The thing that distracts is marked with に, and the sentence usually implies a mistake or oversight followed.

examples.japanese: ⟦スマホ→スマホ：04721_sumaho⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{気|き}を{取|と}られて⟦いた→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: My attention was on my phone.

examples.japanese: ⟦{話|はなし}→話：01496_hanashi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{気|き}を{取|と}られて⟦{駅|えき}→駅：02180_eki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{乗|の}り{過|す}ごした→乗り過ごす：07928_norisugosu⟧。
examples.english: I was caught up in the conversation and rode past my station.

examples.japanese: ⟦{窓|まど}→窓：02254_mado⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{外|そと}→外：00671_soto⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{気|き}を{取|と}られて、⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{説明|せつめい}→説明：01449_setsumei⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{聞|き}いていなかった→聞く：00483_kiku⟧。
examples.english: My attention was outside the window, so I wasn't listening to the teacher's explanation.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}ども⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{気|き}を{取|と}られて⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧うち⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧、なべ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{吹|ふ}きこぼれてしまった。
examples.english: While my attention was on the children, the pot boiled over.

notes:
STRUCTURE: ⟦{気|き}→気：02199_ki⟧ (attention) + ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧ + ⟦{取|と}られる→取る：00565_toru⟧ (passive of ⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧, to take). The passive is fixed — ⟦{気|き}→気：02199_ki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧ is not used in this sense.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- 〜⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{気|き}を{取|と}られる: to have one's attention taken by ~
- 〜⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{気|き}を{取|と}られて…しまう: to be distracted by ~ and end up doing (something unintended)
- {気|き}を{取|と}られて⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧うち⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧: while one's attention was elsewhere

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{気|き}が{散|ち}る→気が散る：06883_kigachiru⟧: to be distracted — attention scatters generally, with no single cause named
- ⟦ぼんやりする→ぼんやりする：21687_bonyarisuru⟧: to be absent-minded — attention is on nothing at all, rather than pulled elsewhere
